scope.description: Complete three-row deepening tranche for the Champion Road 2000 participation prize source group, emphasizing Johto first-partner tournament memory, gold-foil expansion-symbol identification, bottom-border attendance text, World Hobby Fair and Neo Genesis lookalikes, PokeBoon/Bulbapedia source-route tension, and card-specific illustrator credits.

main_chase_cards.name: Cyndaquil

key_artists.name: Naoyo Kimura
key_artists.why: Kimura's Chikorita gives the trio its soft Grass opening: a small starter card that has to carry both Neo Genesis familiarity and Champion Road event memory.

key_artists.name: Shin-ichi Yoshida
key_artists.why: Yoshida's Cyndaquil sits at the center of the fire line's early TCG personality: small, tense, and ready to flare, now with tournament attendance stamped into the object.

key_artists.name: Hironobu Yoshida
key_artists.why: Yoshida's Totodile makes the Water starter feel unruly and alive, which is exactly why the trio works as a memory of playing Gold and Silver in public.

claims.text: The local release groups Bulbapedia raw source rows 151-153 under the promotion note Champion Road 2000 participation prize.

The group contains the three Johto first partners Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile as contiguous source rows; it should not silently absorb the adjacent Champion Road 2000 3-Man Tournament Corner Berry and Miracle Berry rows 154-155.

Bulbapedia card pages describe the Champion Road print as a Japanese promotional variant for participants in a Champion Road tournament held in January 2000, differing from the regular print by bottom-right Champion Road 2000 Attendance Commemoration text and a gold-foil expansion symbol.
Card-specific pages credit Chikorita to Naoyo Kimura, Cyndaquil to Shin-ichi Yoshida, and Totodile to Hironobu Yoshida; the local raw rows themselves do not surface those credits.

This source group matters because it turns the Johto first-partner trio into event attendance memory: Gold/Silver-era starters, ordinary Neo Genesis art lineage, and a tournament-specific gold-foil mark all pressed into one identity claim.

Agents must preserve Champion Road 2000 participation route, rows 151-153, bottom-border attendance text, gold-foil expansion symbol, card-specific illustrator credits, and the distinction from World Hobby Fair, Neo Genesis, Premium File, Johto First Partner Pack, and adjacent 3-Man Tournament Corner rows.

narrative.human_title: Champion Road 2000 participation prize — Johto starters with a gold tournament mark
narrative.why_it_matters: This trio is lovely because it is almost ordinary until it is not. Chikorita, Cyndaquil, and Totodile are familiar Neo Genesis first partners, but Champion Road turns them into proof-of-presence objects: bottom-border attendance text, a gold-foil expansion symbol, and the feeling that Gold and Silver had just become something you could gather around competitively. The identity burden lives in the small marks, not the character names.

Use seller photos for front/back, bottom-border text, expansion symbol foil, card surface, and condition before any transaction claim.

card_highlights.assembly_note: Chikorita row 151 is the Grass member of the Champion Road 2000 starter trio, recognizable by the Champion Road attendance text and gold-foil symbol rather than the character name alone.
card_highlights.collector_texture_note: Chikorita is the quiet beginning of the trio. It looks like the gentle starter card everyone already knows, which is exactly why the Champion Road marks matter: the tournament is not in the species, it is in the little gold and border details.
